title: 卜算子（我住长江头）
titleEn: Song of Divination (I Live Where the Yangtze Begins)
author: 李之仪
intro: Two lovers live at opposite ends of the Yangtze and never meet, yet they drink from the same river. Simple as a folk song, it ends with a wish that his heart be as true as hers.
analysis: 这首词像一首民歌，语言非常朴素，用的是一个女子的口吻。我住在长江上游，你住在长江下游，天天想你却见不到你，我们一起喝着同一条江的水。一条长江，既是隔开两人的距离，又是连接两人的纽带——见不到面，但喝的是同一江水，心就连在一起了。下阕说：这江水什么时候才会停止流动？这离别的痛苦什么时候才会结束？江水不会停，相思也不会停。最后两句是她的心愿：只希望你的心和我的心一样，我就一定不会辜负这份相思。全词反复出现“长江”“君”“水”，节奏回环，很像唱歌，感情真挚，所以流传很广。
analysisEn: This lyric reads like a folk song, in very plain language, spoken by a woman. I live at the head of the Yangtze, you live at its tail; I think of you every day and never see you — and yet we drink from the same river. The river is two things at once: the distance that keeps them apart, and the thread that ties them together. They cannot meet, but the same water reaches them both, and so do their feelings. In the second half she asks when this river will ever stop flowing, and when this ache of separation will ever end. The answer is in the question: the river never stops, and neither will her longing. The last two lines are her wish: if only your heart is like mine, I will never betray this love. Notice how “Long River”, “you” and “water” keep coming back. That circling repetition gives the poem the rhythm of a song and helps explain why it is still so widely loved.
background: Li Zhiyi (dates uncertain, c. 1048 – c. 1117) was a Northern Song official and a friend of Su Shi. He is said to have written this lyric while in exile at Dangtu, on the Yangtze in today’s Anhui, possibly for a singer who later became his companion.
pronunciation: 词牌“卜算子”：卜 bǔ，子按诗词传统标 zǐ。“定不负”的“负”读 fù。无其他特殊读音。

lines.lit: I live at the head of the Long River,
lines.en: I live where the Yangtze begins,

lines.lit: you live at the tail of the Long River.
lines.en: you live where it meets the sea.

lines.py: rì rì sī jūn bù jiàn jūn
lines.lit: Day after day I think of you and do not see you;
lines.en: Every day I miss you, and never see you,

lines.lit: together we drink the Long River’s water.
lines.en: yet we drink from the same river.

lines.lit: This water — when will it stop?
lines.en: When will this river ever stop?

lines.lit: This sorrow — when will it end?
lines.en: When will this ache ever end?

lines.py: zhǐ yuàn jūn xīn sì wǒ xīn
lines.lit: I only wish your heart were like my heart;
lines.en: If only your heart is like mine,

lines.py: dìng bù fù xiāng sī yì
lines.lit: then surely I will not betray this longing.
lines.en: I will never let this love down.

words.en: the upper reaches of the Yangtze
the lower reaches of the Yangtze

words.note: 古代对人的尊称，今天书面语偶尔还用。

words.en: to drink together / from the same source

words.note: 今天“休息”“休止”还保留这个意思。
古义多指遗憾、离愁，和今天的“恨”（仇恨）不同。
古义：停止。今天“不已”“有加无已”还用。
现代汉语仍用，如“单相思”。

imagery.name: 长江
imagery.zh: 长江一头一尾，把两个人隔得很远；同一条江又把两个人连在一起。
imagery.en: The Yangtze holds the lovers at opposite ends — and the same river connects them.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 江水不停地流，就像相思不停，没有尽头。
imagery.en: The water never stops flowing, just as her longing never ends.
